exposure: increased nuchal translucency (NT) and normal karyotype
outcome: prevalence of associated findings (prior to or after birth)
prevalence of children under therapy at school age
children needing treatment (medications or psychopedagogical intervention) at school age
cohort: The study included all singleton pregnancies referred for 1st trimester screening for Down syndrome between January 2004 and December 2006, specifically analyzing cases with NT >95th percentiles who undertook fetal karyotype.
finding: Among fetuses with increased NT and normal karyotype confirmed to be isolated, 3.7% were under treatment at school age, and if detailed ultrasound scans during pregnancy and pediatric evaluation at birth are normal, the risk of adverse outcome at school age is comparable to the general population.
